primary_sources: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, annual average unemployment rates and CPI changes, 1970-1980

source: original; stimulus table compiled from U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics annual averages

stimulus.source_note: Table compiled from U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics annual averages: unemployment rates and Consumer Price Index changes, 1970-1980. Account drawn from the grounding books (Barron's Ch. 10, Topic 8.14; 5 Steps Ch. 28; Princeton Ch. 12).
stimulus.text:
Inflation and unemployment, annual averages (U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics):

| Year | Inflation (change in consumer prices) | Unemployment rate |
| 1970 | 5.7% | 4.9% |
| 1974 | 11.0% | 5.6% |
| 1975 | 9.1% | 8.5% |
| 1979 | 11.3% | 5.8% |
| 1980 | 13.5% | 7.1% |

stem: Which conclusion needs two or more rows of the table together?

options.text: Inflation reached 11 percent in 1974 and 1979, while unemployment stayed below 6 percent.
In 1975, unemployment reached 8.5 percent while inflation was 9.1 percent that year.
options.misconception: That is one row of the table, not a conclusion built from two or more rows.

options.text: In 1980, inflation reached 13.5 percent while unemployment was 7.1 percent that year.
options.misconception: That is one row of the table, not a conclusion built from two or more rows.

options.text: In 1974, inflation reached 11.0 percent while unemployment was 5.6 percent that year.
options.misconception: That is one row of the table, not a conclusion built from two or more rows.

rationales.A: Compare 1974 with 1979: inflation stood at 11.0 percent and then 11.3 percent, while unemployment stayed below 6 percent in both years, so a high-inflation year did not have to be a high-unemployment year.
rationales.B: That fact comes from the 1975 row alone, so it does not need two or more rows.
rationales.C: That fact comes from the 1980 row alone, so it does not need two or more rows.
rationales.D: That fact comes from the 1974 row alone, so it does not need two or more rows.
rationales.general:
1. A single row gives a single fact, and options B, C, and D each repeat one row.
2. Option A compares rows: unemployment was 5.6 percent in 1974 and 5.8 percent in 1979.
3. Inflation was 11.0 percent in 1974 and 11.3 percent in 1979, so high inflation did not need high unemployment.
Remember: A conclusion that compares rows is stronger than a fact copied from one row.
